questions.question: Pile A has red triangles. Pile B has blue circles. What two things sort the piles?
questions.explain: Red vs blue is colour, and triangle vs circle is shape. Both are different, so both sort the piles. A common trap is naming size when both piles are the same size.

questions.question: Pile A has big red squares. Pile B has small blue squares. What two things sort the piles?
questions.explain: Both piles have squares, so shape is the same and does not sort them. Big-vs-small is size and red-vs-blue is colour. A common trap is naming shape when it is the same in both.

questions.question: Pile A has red circles. Pile B has blue squares. What two things sort the piles?
questions.explain: Red vs blue is colour, and circle vs square is shape. Both are different, so both sort the piles. A common trap is naming size when the problem does not mention it.

questions.question: A child puts big red triangles in one pile and small blue triangles in the other. What two things sort the piles?
questions.explain: Both piles have triangles, so shape is the same. Big-vs-small is size and red-vs-blue is colour. A common trap is naming shape when it is the same in both piles.

questions.question: Sam has red triangles, red circles, blue triangles, and blue circles. He makes two piles: all red shapes and all blue shapes. What is his sorting rule?
questions.explain: Both piles have triangles AND circles, so shape does not separate them. Only red-vs-blue (colour) sorts the two piles. A common trap is adding shape when it is the same in both.

questions.question: Lily sorts shapes for art. Group 1: red triangles. Group 2: blue squares. Her friend says, 'You sorted by colour and shape.' Is the friend right?
options: No, colour and size sort them
Yes, colour and shape sort them
No, shape and how big sort them
No, only the colour sorts them
questions.explain: Red vs blue is colour, and triangle vs square is shape. Both are different, so the friend is right. A common trap is naming size when the problem does not mention it.

questions.question: Max sorts shapes. Pile 1: big red circles. Pile 2: small blue circles. His friend says, 'You sorted by size and colour.' Is the friend right?
options: No, size and shape sort them
Yes, size and colour sort them
No, colour and shape sort them
questions.explain: Both piles have circles, so shape is the same. Big-vs-small is size and red-vs-blue is colour, so the friend is right. A common trap is naming shape when it is the same in both.

questions.question: A teacher shows two piles. Pile 1: 3 red triangles. Pile 2: 4 red squares. The teacher says, 'I sorted by colour and shape.' Is she right?
options: Yes, colour and shape sort them
No, size and colour sort them
questions.explain: Both piles are red, so colour does not separate them. Triangle-vs-square is the only thing that sorts the piles. A common trap is trusting a stated rule without checking if it fits.

questions.question: A child sorts 5 red triangles, 3 blue triangles, 4 red circles, and 2 blue circles into 4 piles. Her friend says, 'You only sorted by colour.' Is the friend right?
options: No, colour and shape sort them
Yes, only the colour sorts them
No, shape and size sort them
No, colour and size sort them
questions.explain: There are triangle piles AND circle piles, and red piles AND blue piles. Both colour and shape sort them. A common trap is naming one attribute and stopping.

questions.question: A teacher has 3 big red circles, 4 big blue circles, and 2 small red circles. She makes 3 piles sorted by size and colour. A child says, 'You also sorted by shape.' Is the child right?
options: Yes, shape and size sort them
questions.explain: Every shape is a circle, so shape is the same in all piles. Size and colour are the real rules. A common trap is adding an attribute that does not change between groups.

questions.question: Noah sorts stickers. Box A has big square stickers, and Box B has small circle stickers. He finds a big circle sticker. Where does it go?
options: Box A, since it is big
Box B, since it is round
questions.explain: Box A needs big squares and Box B needs small circles. A big circle matches only half of each rule, so it fits neither box.

questions.question: Sara makes two groups. Group 1 has a big red square, a big red circle, and a big red triangle. Group 2 has small blue shapes. What two things did she sort by?
questions.explain: Group 1 is big and red, and Group 2 is small and blue. The shapes are mixed inside Group 1, so shape is not part of her rule.

questions.question: All of Owen's blocks are yellow. Tray 1 has big squares and Tray 2 has small triangles. Owen says, 'I sorted by colour and size.' What is wrong?
questions.explain: Every block is yellow, so colour cannot tell the two trays apart. Owen really sorted by size and shape.

questions.question: Amir has 2 big triangles, 3 small triangles, and 2 big squares. He puts the big shapes with 3 sides in a bag. How many shapes go in the bag?
questions.explain: Big shapes with 3 sides means big triangles, and there are 2 of them. Counting all 5 triangles or all 4 big shapes uses only one attribute.
